title: Moving out
topic: A seller refunds more than the sale and lets the buyer keep the lamp, then counts only the $5 cash gap
blurb: A friend sold a lamp, then paid to end the argument, and thinks it only cost five dollars.
prompt: A friend just texted this in the group chat. If one line doesn't add up, tap it.

segments.label: The sale
segments.text: Sold my desk lamp for $30 on Marketplace before moving out.

segments.label: The text
segments.text: The buyer Venmo'd me, then messaged that the switch felt loose.

segments.label: The send-back
segments.text: Didn't want drama on moving day, so I sent him $35 and told him to just keep the lamp.

segments.label: The shrug
segments.text: Annoying, but honestly worth losing $5 just to be done with it.

conclusion: Sent $35 back on a $30 sale, so it only cost $5 to make the hassle go away.

flaws.original: That's not losing $5. I refunded $35 and let him keep a $30 lamp — I'm out the lamp and $5 cash.
flaws.corrupted: Annoying, but honestly worth losing $5 just to be done with it.

diagnosis_choices.label: You also let him keep the $30 lamp. You're out the lamp and $5 cash, not just $5.
Venmo takes a fee, so the real cash loss is a bit more than $5.
A used lamp wasn't really worth $30, so the $5 already overstates the loss.
The only mistake is the extra $5. Sending back $30 and letting him keep it would have been even.

fix_choices.label: Admit you're out a $30 lamp and $5 cash — or get the lamp back.
Ask him to send $5 so the cash evens out, and he can keep the lamp.
Retcon the sale price as $35, so the refund becomes a wash.
Count the original $30 as profit, which cancels the $35 you sent back.

flaws.explanation: You're out $5 in cash — and you no longer have a lamp.
flaws.why_tempting: Watching $30 come in and $35 go out leaves a tidy $5 in your head. The lamp quietly leaves the ledger.
flaws.catch_rule: If you refund the money and let them keep the thing, you've lost the thing too — not just the difference.
flaws.hint: After this, who has the lamp? And who has the $35?

practice.problem: You sell a used bike for $80. The buyer complains, so you send $90 and say keep it. A friend says, 'So you only lost $10.' What's missing?
practice.answer: You also no longer have the bike. You're out the bike and $10, not just $10.

clean_segments: Sold my desk lamp for $30 on Marketplace before moving out.
The buyer Venmo'd me, then messaged that the switch felt loose.
Didn't want drama on moving day, so I sent him $35 and told him to just keep the lamp.
That's not losing $5. I refunded $35 and let him keep a $30 lamp — I'm out the lamp and $5 cash.
clean_conclusion: You didn't just lose $5. You gave back the money and the lamp.
